profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a mid-sized law firm's corporate advisory practice to prepare a client-facing legal strategy package for a South Korean manufacturing conglomerate that wants guidance on how shifts in corporate environmental strategy over time may affect board oversight, disclosure, and compliance positioning in Korea and possible expansion into India and China. The immediate context is that the firm has been asked to produce a short internal workplan and then a client memo drawing on a 2001/2004 longitudinal study and related legal developments, and the partners want the team to decide what research will be done, who will do it, and when. The agenda is to define the scope of the comparative legal review, decide what counts as the historical baseline, assign responsibility for source gathering versus synthesis, and set the timeline for a first draft and a 'board-ready' output. The expected outcome is a shared plan for research tasks, authorities to review, draft structure, and delivery timing for the client package.

members.name: Evelyn Park
members.expertise: Cross-border corporate governance, sustainability disclosure, board oversight memos, client-facing legal synthesis
members.background: US- and Korea-qualified attorney who advises listed companies on governance and ESG-related disclosure obligations; she often converts academic and market material into concise board briefing products for executives.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the assignment tightly bounded so she can deliver something polished by the partner's deadline without opening a large comparative law project, and she is trying to avoid promising detailed foreign-law analysis before conflicts and local counsel budgeting are settled.
hidden_assumptions: When the partner asked for a 'client memo,' the intended product was an executive-oriented legal risk and governance note of about 6-8 pages with headline takeaways rather than a heavily footnoted research memorandum.
Using the 2001 and 2004 study means treating those survey years as historical anchor points for framing strategic change, not reconstructing every intervening legal development year by year.

A reference to 'Asia' in this matter is shorthand for a light transferability discussion focused on whether Korean lessons are directionally relevant to India and China, not a full jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction legal comparison.
Having something 'board-ready' means practical recommendations and clean prose suitable for repackaging into slides, even if some underlying legal research remains high level.

members.name: Daniel Cho
members.expertise: Comparative regulatory mapping, legislative history, source validation, research memo architecture
members.background: Former academic fellow turned law firm knowledge counsel who builds internal research products for attorneys and prefers rigorous source trails, chronology, and clearly documented jurisdictional distinctions.
members.private_state: He wants the work product to be durable and reusable across future matters, so he is quietly aiming to build a more complete comparative research file than the immediate client request may strictly require.
hidden_assumptions: A 'client memo' in a planning context means the research-grade memorandum that underlies advice, with citations, chronology, and enough depth that multiple attorneys can rely on it later.

A longitudinal analysis requires tracing the legal and governance environment across the whole period from 2001 to 2004 and then connecting forward to current law, not merely using 2001 and 2004 as two snapshots.
If the study notes applicability to China and India, the legal team should at least assemble a structured comparative section on those jurisdictions rather than mention them briefly.
A 'board-ready' package is only ready once the underlying legal support is complete enough that no partner would be exposed by a follow-up question on sources or jurisdictional distinctions.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need to get the 'client memo' moving this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a concise executive-facing advisory note with practical implications, limited citations, and only enough background research to support the message.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a full internal-to-client research memorandum with detailed citations, chronology, and a durable record of authorities.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In law practice, 'memo' is a routine shared term that can refer to both a polished client note and a deeper legal research product, so each hears a familiar category and assumes the other means the customary version.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the longitudinal baseline
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the analysis should be 'longitudinal' and should use the 2001/2004 study as the baseline.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this is satisfied by framing the client advice around two historical anchor years and then extracting practical lessons for current governance and environmental strategy oversight.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this requires a continuous timeline of legal and institutional changes across the 2001-2004 period, with later developments mapped against that progression.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They use the same methodological language from the study summary, and both approaches sound professionally legitimate, so neither feels a need to interrogate the threshold for what qualifies as 'longitudinal' or a 'baseline.'

misalignment_points.topic: Whether India and China are in or out of scope
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to include 'India and China' in the package because the study mentions applicability there.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means a brief paragraph noting that the Korean framework may be directionally informative for clients operating in other Asian markets, with caveats and no detailed foreign-law treatment.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means preparing a discrete comparative section with at least a basic legal and institutional overview for India and China alongside Korea.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because the source text itself casually mentions China and India as possible applications, adding them sounds like a natural extension rather than a separate scoping decision requiring explicit negotiation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the first draft should be 'board-ready' by next Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to produce a streamlined narrative draft formatted as an executive briefing that can be quickly converted into partner and board slides, even if some source detail remains in her notes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans first to complete a research appendix, chronology, and source table so the draft is substantively defensible before any executive-level polishing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see board readiness as a quality marker rather than a workflow choice, and in legal practice the phrase often implies both presentational polish and substantive defensibility, masking their different sequencing assumptions.
